uncited: Unlike [Normal Approximation with Finite Differences](9736-normal-approximation-with-finite-differences.md), which computes gradients on-the-fly from scalar data, this method relies on a pre-computed grid of normals, offering a trade-off between memory usage and runtime gradient calculation cost.
- The normal grid is stored as three separate 3D arrays (one for each component) or a single 3D array of 3D vectors.
**Retrieve Corner Normals:** Identify the 8 corner normals of the voxel containing the point.
In some contexts, the "normals" are derived from gradients of scalar amplitude data $F$.
It differs by explicitly deriving the corner normals from the gradients of scalar amplitude data $F$ using central finite differences before interpolation.
It is chosen when the volume data is scalar and smooth, and high-quality lighting is required without storing a separate normal grid.
- **When to use:** When high-quality shading is needed and pre-computed normals are available or gradients are cheap to compute.
